Cindy Holscher

Democratic candidate for Governor / Lieutenant Governor, Kansas · Open seat

Kansas state senator (District 8); formerly worked for Sprint

Cindy Holscher is a Democratic state senator from Overland Park who has represented Kansas Senate District 8 since 2021, after serving two terms in the Kansas House (2017–2021). She won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for governor with 48.7% of the vote, defeating state Sen. Ethan Corson and Overland Park Mayor Curt Skoog. She faces Republican Ty Masterson in the November 3, 2026 general election, with state Rep. KC Ohaebosim as her running mate.

Where Holscher stands

Medicaid expansion
Supports expanding Medicaid. She says rural hospitals in Kansas are six times more likely to close without it and plans to seek bipartisan support to pass it.
Property taxes
Proposes cutting local property taxes by having the state fully fund K-12 special education and by limiting property tax exemptions and economic development deals that she says shift the tax burden onto homeowners.
Public education
Supports full state funding of special education in K-12 public schools.
Data centers
Supports pausing approval of new data centers in Kansas until guardrails are in place.
Marijuana
Supports legalizing recreational marijuana in Kansas.
Abortion
Supports abortion rights. She opposed the 2022 constitutional amendment on abortion, which Kansas voters rejected.
Judicial selection
Opposed the August 2026 constitutional amendment that would have required Kansas Supreme Court justices to be elected. Voters rejected it.
Income taxes
Voted in 2017 to repeal the 2012 state income tax cuts. She argues that tax breaks for corporations and wealthy interests have shifted too much of the tax burden onto working families.
Stadium subsidies
Voted to authorize negotiations to bring the Royals or Chiefs to Kansas but opposed the final Chiefs deal, which included $1.8 billion in state bonds. She said billionaires should fund their own stadiums.
